8. Petitioner was then telegraphically-asked to appear before respondent No. 1 on 25-11-66 and the petitioner duly appeared. It was alleged, that practically no opportunity was given to him to explain his case in details. Thereafter the petitioner was compulsorily retired from service with effect from 6-12-76 by a letter dated 11.12.76 communicated by respondent No. 2 Copy of the letter of compulsory retirement is marked Annexure up" to the petition. Annexure 'a' is the letter' from the acting Principal directing the petitioner to vacate the quarters by and January, 1977 and in intimating him that he would have three months' salary in lieu of notice and he would get the benefit of Provident Fund. It has been submitted on behalf of the petitioner that the respondent No.1 has applied his judicial mind to 'the report of the Inquiry Officer the causes showily the petitioner which if considered in proper perspective the petitioner would have been absolved  of the charge. It has further been submitted that statement of the allegations on which the charge is based and of any other circumstances which the authority proposing to take into consideration when passing orders in the case were not communicated to the petitioner along with the charge framed and this has violated 'the mandatory requirement of Rule 5 (e)(i) of the Rules. It was also submitted that the petitioner was not allowed to be present before the Inquiry Officer while the examination-in-chief of the three witnesses, namely Mr. Mofazzal Hossain, Vice-Principal Major Rezaul Haider, Adjutant, and Major Masudul Abedin former Adjutant were taken. After the conclusion of examination-in-chief of the aforesaid three witnesses, the petitioner was allowed to enter into the room when the Inquiry Officer showed him written testimony of those witnesses, and did not allow him sufficient time to read the deposition and to cross-examine the witnesses. It was submit fed that no opportunity as provided under, Rule 5(e)(ii) of the Rules to cross-examine the witness was afforded to the petitioner. It was further submitted that copy of the full report as required under Rule 5(e)(v) was not supplied to the petitioner along with the second show cause notice and as' such he failed to submit a comprehensive reply to the said show cause notice. 

 1. (b) That you admitted Cadet No. 613 Rabiul Alam S/o. Chief Manager HBFC, and Cadet No. 616 Kazi Shafiur Rahman S/o. Another Officer HBFC in irregular manner with a view to getting undue favour and wrongful gain from the fathers of these cadets in the matter of purchase of a house at Binodpur at an abnormally low price and that amount to misconduct and corruption as defined in Regulation 2(b) and (c) of the aforesaid Regulations. 

 Alongwith the said charge was enclosed copy of Respondent Nos. 2 letter dated 6th April, 1976 and it was stated therein that the petitioner may be charged on account of admitting sub caliber students for his personal gain. This was explained as follows:- The Son of Chief Manager, HBFC, Rajshahi, Cadet No. 613 Rabiul Alam and Son of another officer of HBFC, cadet No. 616 Kazi Safiur Rahman were admitted and in return the grateful guardian procured a house at Binodpur at a cost of Tk. 53,000/- only which otherwise would cost him a minimum of Tk. 2,50,000/-. No other statement of the allegation on which the said charges was based was communicated to the petitioner. The statement of allegations does not show how the petitioner admitted the two cadets in irregular manner nor does it state particulars which would show that the price of the house was abnormally low. 

 15. As regards the second contention of the learned Advocate for the petitioner that the petitioner was not given fair opportunity to cross-examine the witnesses we have perused the order sheet of the inquiry officer and the depositions recorded the petitioner's contention was that he was not allowed to remain present when the three witnesses viz. P.W. 1 Vice Principal in Charge Mr. Mofazzal Hossain, Major Rezaul Haider, Adjutant and Major Masudul Abedin, former Adjutant were examined and that after the conclusion of the Examination-in-Chief the petitioner was allowed to enter in to the room. It was not specifically controverted in the affidavit-in-opposition although it was denied that Inquiry Officer obstructed the petitioner in cross-examining the said witnesses.
